text: The sources do not fully agree on the 2012 tree-cover loss on this property. The Hansen Global Forest Change dataset (GFC-2025-v1.13) observed a tree-cover loss of 1.4 hectares in 2012. However, the JRC Global Forest Cover 2020 dataset (GFC2020 V4) only corroborates 51% of this area as forest in 2020, which meets the minimum threshold for agreement. The Uruguay Ministry of Livestock, Agriculture and Fisheries (MGAP) forest map from 2021 indicates that the area of loss was not native forest but rather planted forest, specifically Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda. Therefore, while there is some agreement, the sources differ in the specifics of the forest type and the extent of the loss.
